content: The interaction between mesalamine and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may lead to an increase in the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of mesalamine by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while metaproterenol decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. The combination of methazolamide and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can lead to increased plasma levels of both drugs due to mutual inhibition of renal tubular secretion. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (CAIs) also shift salicylates from plasma to the central nervous system, potentially causing neurotoxicity. Close monitoring is necessary. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of methotrexate by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Salicylates can reduce methotrexate clearance, especially during high-dose methotrexate therapy, increasing the risk of toxicity. Even at low methotrexate doses, caution is warranted, and close monitoring is essential. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while methylclothiazide decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Additionally, methylclothiazide may increase the levels or effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), which are pH-dependent, coadministration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Separating the administration of antacids and methylphenidate extended-release capsules is advised. The combination of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and methylprednisolone may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Close monitoring is recommended. Methylprednisolone may also decrease the levels of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while metolazone decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Additionally, metolazone may increase the levels or effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of metoprolol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin) may also increase serum potassium levels when combined with metoprolol. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate is contraindicated with mifepristone due to the risk of excessive bleeding caused by aspirin-induced antiplatelet activity. This interaction is serious and should be avoided. The combination of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and milnacipran may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. There is an increased risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding, as SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Close monitoring is necessary. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases anticoagulation, while mistletoe decreases it. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of moexipril by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce the synthesis of vasodilating renal prostaglandins, affecting fluid homeostasis and potentially diminishing the antihypertensive effect of moexipril. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of moxisylyte by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and nabumetone both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may also increase the levels or effects of nabumetone by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of nadolol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin) may also increase serum potassium levels when combined with nadolol. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and nafcillin may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Close monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and naproxen both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may also increase the levels or effects of naproxen by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of nebivolol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin) may also increase serum potassium levels when combined with nebivolol. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of neomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants. Close monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Separating the administration of antacids and neratinib by 3 hours is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases anticoagulation, while nettle decreases it. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Administering antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib can avoid this interaction. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may enhance the pharmacological effects of nitroglycerin when administered concomitantly. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and noni juice both increase serum potassium levels. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while norepinephrine decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. The combination of ofloxacin and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may increase the risk of central nervous system stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from its receptors in the brain. Close monitoring is necessary. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of olmesartan by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce the synthesis of vasodilating renal prostaglandins, affecting fluid homeostasis and potentially diminishing the antihypertensive effect of olmesartan. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Both olmesartan and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separating the dosing of tetracyclines from these products is advised. Patients taking omega-3 fatty acids and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate should be monitored periodically due to the potential increased risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and oxacillin may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Close monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and oxaprozin both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may also increase the levels or effects of oxaprozin by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and panax ginseng both increase anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and parecoxib both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may also increase the levels or effects of parecoxib by competing for renal tubular clearance as acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of paromomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants. Close monitoring is recommended. The combination of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and paroxetine may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. There is an increased risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding, as SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Close monitoring is necessary. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and pau d'arco both increase anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Pegaspargase increases the effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of bleeding events. Close monitoring is necessary. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of pemetrexed through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Interrupting NSAID dosing with long elimination half-lives for at least 5 days before, the day of, and 2 days following pemetrexed administration is recommended. If coadministration of an NSAID is necessary, patients should be closely monitored for toxicity, particularly myelosuppression, renal toxicity, and gastrointestinal toxicity. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of penbutolol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin) may also increase serum potassium levels when combined with penbutolol. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and penicillin G aqueous may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Close monitoring is recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of penicillin VK by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. The combination of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and pentazocine may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Chronic therapy may pose a possible risk of renal papillary necrosis. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of perindopril by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce the synthesis of vasodilating renal prostaglandins, affecting fluid homeostasis and potentially diminishing the antihypertensive effect of perindopril. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Separating pexidartinib dosing by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and phenindione both increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of phenoxybenzamine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of phentolamine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Close monitoring is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and phytoestrogens both increase anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of pindolol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin) may also increase serum potassium levels when combined with pindolol. Caution and monitoring are advised. Piperacillin increases the levels or effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by plasma protein binding competition. Close monitoring is recommended.
